text:
Paris, and this is a day in '59, in the air.
It seems the same radiant day has lasted ever since.
Spring knows what it is doing with its kisses. I am still looking for you
in that hurried taxi, among the crowd. It is written that tonight
I will sleep a long time beside your body, and the endless train.

Paris, and this is the match of fierce wonder.
Everything happens in the flash and we have burned without stopping from the start
in our surfeit. Let us love one another through these poor minutes.
The gods stitched us from trains and more trains and wandering planes,
and from ships and ships, this net that binds us on earth.

Paris, and this the sudden swell of eternity.
There we said goodbye so we could keep flying. Do not forget
to write to me. The loss of this skin, these hands,
and those terrible wheels that carry you so far into the night,
and this world opening beneath us so it can go on being born.

Paris, and we go together in the joyful whirl
of this that is born and born with each day's revolution.
To your tall petals I entrust the star of the one who comes in the months of your blood,
and I leave you sleeping on the sheet. I put my hand on the beauty
of your pregnancy, and plainly touch the source.

translation.title: The Lovers
